summary: Command & Conquer entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2
entries.definitive_edition: Steam/EA app package with Yuri's Revenge installed

emulation.notes: Native Windows route with compatibility fixes as needed.

primary.version: Current Steam/EA app package with Yuri's Revenge
primary.why: Red Alert 2 is a Windows RTS, and the current Steam/EA package includes Yuri's Revenge as the practical modern purchase/install route. There are compatibility caveats, so renderer/patch state should be part of the archive notes.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam or EA app package, include Yuri's Revenge for a complete route, and record renderer, compatibility fixes, resolution, patch state, and whether multiplayer is official, LAN, or community-hosted.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a remaster. Record renderer, compatibility fixes, and whether community multiplayer services are used.

entries.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Remastered Collection at current patch level

primary.why: The Remastered Collection includes Red Alert, its expansions, console mission content, rebuilt multiplayer, bonus gallery material, and 4K remastered presentation, making it the current official completeness/fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Use Command & Conquer Remastered Collection on PC. Record storefront/build, classic vs remastered graphics toggle, expansion/console missions played, mods, multiplayer state, and whether original DOS/Windows behavior is being compared.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record classic/remastered toggle, mod use, and multiplayer/service state.

entries.title: Command & Conquer

emulation.emulator: DOSBox/original Windows only for historical comparison
emulation.notes: Native PC remaster is the main route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Remastered Collection at current patch level, with original build comparison if desired

primary.why: The Remastered Collection is the current official route for Tiberian Dawn, with remastered presentation, classic toggle, expansion material, console mission content, multiplayer, bonus gallery material, and mod support. It is the best one-route archive target for the 1995 original.
primary.how_to_play: Use Command & Conquer Remastered Collection on PC. Record storefront/build, classic/remastered graphics toggle, expansion/console missions played, mods, multiplayer state, and whether the DOS/Windows original was compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original Westwood behavior and period PC presentation
secondary.what_to_play: Use only for a historical comparison against the remaster.
secondary.why: The remaster is the current completeness/fidelity route, but original behavior can matter for preservation notes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record classic/remastered toggle, mod use, and multiplayer/service state.

entries.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC final-patch base game, with Uprising tracked separately

emulation.notes: Use native PC route for the base game.

primary.why: The PC release is the cleanest capture and control route for Red Alert 3's co-op campaign, skirmish, and mod/settings ecosystem. The PlayStation 3 Ultimate Edition has bonus material, while Uprising is a separate standalone expansion to track alongside the base game.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows PC version from Steam or EA App with the final patch. Record storefront, patch/build, DRM/account state, co-op availability, map/mod state, and whether Uprising or PS3 Ultimate Edition bonus material was checked separately.

secondary.what_to_play: Inspect only if documenting platform-specific extras.
secondary.why: It is not the best capture route, but it has edition-specific bonus content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Standalone expansion with Commander's Challenge and new single-player content
secondary.what_to_play: Track as a separate expansion route after the base game.
secondary.why: It is a standalone follow-up, not a replacement for the base campaign.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record storefront, patch, DRM/account state, and whether co-op or Uprising content is available.

entries.title: Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC final-patch base game, with Kane's Wrath tracked separately

primary.why: The PC release is the main route for Tiberium Wars because it has the intended RTS controls, best capture/settings path, and access to the expansion and mod ecosystem. The Xbox 360 route is a console adaptation, while Kane's Wrath should be tracked as a separate expansion.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows PC version with final patch. Record storefront, patch/build, mod/map state, multiplayer/service state, and whether Kane's Wrath was played afterward.

secondary.exclusive_content: Standalone expansion campaign, factions, and Global Conquest mode
secondary.what_to_play: Track as expansion content after the base campaign/skirmish route.
secondary.why: It extends Tiberium Wars but is a separate expansion entry, not a replacement.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record patch, storefront, mod/map state, and multiplayer/service availability.

entries.title: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun
entries.definitive_edition: Tiberian Sun plus Firestorm on current PC package or CnCNet-compatible install

emulation.emulator: Not required; use Windows compatibility, cnc-ddraw, or VM if needed
emulation.notes: Prefer current PC package with documented fixes; CnCNet for online multiplayer.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows retail plus Firestorm on period-correct hardware, or fixed modern PC route for capture

primary.version: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun and Firestorm, current Steam/EA or CnCNet-fixed route
primary.why: Tiberian Sun is Windows-only and its Firestorm expansion adds important campaign and unit content. The current archive route should include Firestorm and use either the current official Steam/EA package or the CnCNet/freeware route with compatibility fixes documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam/EA Ultimate Collection release or CnCNet-compatible install with Firestorm. Record source, version, renderer, resolution, cnc-ddraw/CnCNet client state, campaign order, multiplayer service state, and whether FMV/audio or original disc behavior differs.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original installer, disc, FMV/audio, and patch baseline
secondary.what_to_play: Use only if documenting period-correct behavior.
secondary.why: Modern Windows usually needs fixes or the current official/freeware route.

secondary.exclusive_content: Modern online multiplayer and compatibility wrapper
secondary.why: It is a community access layer rather than the original retail state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record renderer, compatibility wrapper, source package, FMV/audio state, and multiplayer client. Do not confuse with Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars.

entries.title: Command & Conquer: Renegade
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC original with patch/scripts/community-server state documented

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC build with current community patch/server state documented

primary.version: Current PC route with Tiberian Technologies/scripts and multiplayer state documented
primary.why: Renegade is a PC-only Command & Conquer FPS, and current preservation depends on PC fixes, community multiplayer infrastructure, and the 2025 source-code/modding context. Renegade X is a separate fan project and should not replace the original.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned/current PC copy through EA App/Steam/collection media where available. Record build, patches/scripts, W3D Hub or community server state, source-code/modding state, single-player difficulty, multiplayer server, and whether Renegade X was only referenced.

secondary.why: It is not the original 2002 Renegade.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not substitute Renegade X for the original game.

entries.title: Command & Conquer 4: Tiberian Twilight
entries.definitive_edition: Steam/EA app Windows release, after verifying EA login and always-online behavior

emulation.notes: Native Windows route only; online/account state is part of the archive record.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Current Windows package with authenticated service state documented

primary.version: Steam/EA app route with account and always-online state verified
primary.why: Tiberian Twilight is a Windows-only Command & Conquer entry, and the current practical route is the Steam/EA app package when it can authenticate. It requires a constant internet connection/account, so archive capture must verify login/server behavior before committing to a run.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam or EA app Windows release if it authenticates successfully. Record storefront, EA account/linking state, patch/build, online requirement, campaign mission, class/crawler loadout, co-op/multiplayer availability, compatibility settings, and any login workaround needed.

secondary.exclusive_content: Launch-era account, key, and server behavior
secondary.what_to_play: Use only if preserved and still authenticates.
secondary.why: The game is service/account dependent; current accessibility can differ from launch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record service/login state. Do not merge with Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars or Tiberian Sun.
